newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's FIS appoints official spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's FIS appoints official spokesman.

text.p: Algeria's outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) appointed an official spokesman on Monday to clarify its political stance and stop what it called attempts to hurt its credibility.
A statement received in Paris from FIS leader-in-exile Rabah Kebir, who is based in Germany, said the job was given to Abdelkrim Ould Dadda, a member of the FIS leadership in exile.

It said Ould Dadda will act as official spokesman to convey the FIS' "unaltered official positions to national and foreign public opinion, efforting to clarify its stands and respond to rumours and speculation designed to distort the image of FIS or try to hurt its credibility".

FIS earlier this month re-appointed Kebir and dropped hardliners Kamerddine Kherbane and Abdallah Anas in a reshuffle apparently intended to distance the leadership from figures known for their direct links with the guerrillas in Algeria.

The FIS was outlawed after 1992 parliamentary elections it was poised to win were scrapped. About 60,000 people have died since then in the strife pitting government forces against Moslem rebels, including the FIS' armed wing Islamic Salvation Army (AIS).

The FIS is banned from running in the parliamentary elections set for June 5. Analysts say it wants to harmonise its stated policy of seeking negotiations with the Algerian authorities with AIS policy of keeping up skirmishes with government forces. The FIS' founding leaders Abassi Madani and Ali Belhaj are in prison in Algeria.
